prompt:
Sales staff want to set stock aside for a customer who is still deciding, before any bill is raised. Today there is no way to do that: the only thing that ties up stock is a finished sale, so while a customer deliberates the same units can be promised to someone else and the business ends up over-committed. Add a way to put a temporary reservation on a quantity of a product for a customer, separate from raising a bill. While such a reservation is in place those units must not be available to anyone else, and there must be a way to let the reservation go again, returning the units to availability. Setting one aside must be all-or-nothing and must never set aside more than is genuinely available.

Implement this in the internal/service package: a HoldService constructed by service.NewHoldService(db). It must expose Place(tenantID, sku string, qty int, createdOn string) (Hold, error) - which reserves qty units of the product for the tenant and returns the created Hold (a struct with a string ID field), or returns an error without changing anything if qty exceeds the product's available stock (available = OnHand - Reserved) - and Release(holdID string) error, which frees that hold's units back to availability.
issue_title: No way to set stock aside for a customer before billing
issue_body:
Sales staff want to set stock aside for a customer who is still deciding, before any bill is raised. Today there is no way to do that: the only thing that ties up stock is a finished sale, so while a customer deliberates the same units can be promised to someone else and the business ends up over-committed. Add a way to put a temporary reservation on a quantity of a product for a customer, separate from raising a bill. While such a reservation is in place those units must not be available to anyone else, and there must be a way to let the reservation go again, returning the units to availability. Setting one aside must be all-or-nothing and must never set aside more than is genuinely available.

Implement this in the internal/service package: a HoldService constructed by service.NewHoldService(db). It must expose Place(tenantID, sku string, qty int, createdOn string) (Hold, error) - which reserves qty units of the product for the tenant and returns the created Hold (a struct with a string ID field), or returns an error without changing anything if qty exceeds the product's available stock (available = OnHand - Reserved) - and Release(holdID string) error, which frees that hold's units back to availability.
expected_behavior: Setting stock aside for a customer reduces what is available by the amount set aside.
Letting a reservation go returns exactly its units to availability, affecting no other reservation.
A reservation that asks for more than is available is refused and changes nothing.
Stock already set aside cannot be set aside again by another reservation.
Expose service.HoldService (via service.NewHoldService(db)) with Place(tenantID, sku, qty, createdOn) (Hold, error) and Release(holdID) error; a Hold carries a string ID.
expected_failure_summary: The broken snapshot has no concept of a temporary stock reservation: only a completed sale ties up stock, so there is no way to set units aside for a customer and release them, and concurrent commitments can over-promise the same units.
task_author_notes: Stage 1 of the bizflow_holds group. Reference adds a holds concept: a 0003_holds migration creating the holds table (id, tenant_id, sku, quantity, created_at), a repository.HoldRepo (internal/repository/holds.go) with Insert/Get/ListByTenant/All/SetQuantity/Delete, a store.Table.Delete helper (internal/store/table.go), and a service.HoldService (internal/service/holds.go) exposing Place/Release/List. Placing a hold reserves stock (increments products.reserved) and records a hold row inside a single transaction; releasing frees it. The clean lever for Stage 2: a private consume(holdID, units, fulfil) helper and a model.Hold record carrying quantity, so expiry (release filtered by time) and partial fulfillment (a quantity-parameterized consume that also draws down on_hand) are cheap additions rather than a rewrite. The hidden check.go imports bizflow/internal/service and calls NewHoldService: on broken HoldService is undefined so it fails to compile; on gold it compiles and the behavioural assertions pass. The visible test imports only stable bizdb/repository/service packages unchanged by holds, so it runs on both snapshots.
